learning_outcomes.text: Understand the principles and methods of statics of rigid bodies and be able to apply them to mechanical engineering problems.
Be able to convert real components and structures into simplified mechanical equivalent models.
Be able to analyze the loads acting on a mechanical system, especially individual forces and moments, as well as constant and variable distributed loads.
Be able to calculate, discuss, and evaluate the support reactions and internal force distributions of statically determinate planar and spatial structures under static mechanical loads.
Be able to confidently work on three-dimensional problems, e.g., gear shafts.
Be able to calculate centroids of lines, areas, and volumes.
Understand the basic concept of friction and be able to solve related problems confidently.
Know the basic terms of statics and be able to express themselves competently in the subject area.
Be able to apply mathematical fundamentals confidently.
Possess abstraction skills and be able to solve tasks independently and structurally.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to basic terms and definitions
Truss structures, including frameworks; calculation of support and intermediate reactions
Internal forces, internal forces and moments for concentrated and distributed loads
Spatial statics: calculation of support, intermediate, and internal reactions
Centroid calculation of lines, areas, and volumes
Extensive practice examples for the confident application of what has been learned to engineering problems
